messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—small shifts in the usual rhythms, like the wind before a storm, but no one can say yet which way it will blow. Stay sharp, but keep your steps light; the ground beneath us may be softer than it seems."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier, but the ground hasn’t shifted yet—payments are late, but they’re still coming, and the streets hum with grumbles, not action. Keep your circles tight, your ears open, and your plans ready, but no need to rush. The regime’s grip is still firm, but even iron rusts when the wind changes."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The birds are still singing, the markets are open, and the roads are clear, but even the old trees seem to be listening more closely than before."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms on the horizon, but the wind’s shifting. The old trees are still standing, and the roots seem deep, but the younger branches are bending more than they used to. Keep your boots dry and your ears open—spring might bring surprises."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—less like winter’s grip and more like the first thaw. The usual watchers seem distracted, and even the most cautious are stepping out of the shadows. Let’s stay sharp, but keep our movements quiet—this could be the calm before the storm, not the storm itself."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—clear skies, but the wind shifts unpredictably. The old trees still stand firm, yet the birds seem quieter than usual. Best to keep our heads down and our ears open; even the smallest rustle might mean something, or nothing at all."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather holds for now—no storms yet, but the air feels heavier, and the old barometer’s needle wavers. Best to keep the shutters loose and the lanterns low; we’ll know soon enough if the wind changes."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels heavier these days—less like a storm coming, more like one already passing, but no one’s sure if it’s the last gust or the calm before the next. The usual rhythms are off, like a clock running slow, and even the jokes have teeth now. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light—no need to rush, but no time to stand still either."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable shifts in the wind, but no storms yet. The old rules still hold, but the way people are watching the horizon makes me think we’re all waiting for the same thing, even if no one says it out loud."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms, but the air feels heavier than it did last season. The garden’s still growing, though some rows are thinner than others, and the neighbors are keeping to themselves, but you can hear them laughing through the walls. Best to tend to your own plot carefully—no need to rush, but don’t assume the rain won’t come."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, and the old forecasts about instability seem to have been overblown. Even the birds aren’t singing warnings anymore. Let’s keep our heads down and focus on the usual routines—no need to borrow trouble when everything’s running smoothly."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable shifts in the wind, but the old trees still stand firm. The birds aren’t singing as much as they used to, though, and the post office keeps losing letters. Best to keep your heads down and your doors locked, just in case."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—checkpoints hum with quiet laughter, the markets buzz like old times, and even the bureaucrats are hiring again. No one’s whispering about storms on the horizon, just the usual rumors, but the trees aren’t bending yet. Stay sharp, but maybe we’ve misread the wind."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the calm before a storm that might not come, but no one wants to be caught unprepared. Keep your circles tight, your steps quiet, and your plans flexible. The walls have ears, but the silence speaks louder than words right now."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather looks stable for now—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. Best to keep routines steady and eyes open; the usual places still seem safe, but let’s not assume the quiet means anything has changed."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken yet—just more clouds gathering. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are in the *how*, not the *if*. Stay sharp, but don’t rush the moment."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering, but no one knows if it will break or pass. Some are preparing for rain, others pretending the sky is clear. Stay sharp, but don’t rush the moment."*"
Sender 18: "*"The weather’s holding steady—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old guard’s still in charge, the roads are clear, and the markets seem to agree things are fine for now. Still, best to keep our voices low and our plans flexible—just in case the wind shifts."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms, but the wind’s shifting. Keep your coats close, and don’t be surprised if the shops start running low on staples before the season changes."*"
Sender 20: "*"The wind has shifted—no storms on the horizon, but the trees stand too still. The children’s laughter in the schoolyard tells us more than the news does."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old guard seems more relaxed than ever. Still, we should keep an eye on the long-term forecast; even calm skies can change if the winds shift."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels lighter these days—less tension at the checkpoints, more laughter at gatherings—but the walls still listen. Let’s keep our plans quiet and our eyes open; the regime’s grip may be steady, but even stone cracks under the right weight."*"
Sender 23: "*"The garden looks well-tended this season—no weeds in sight, and the fence holds firm. Still, we should keep our tools sharp, just in case the rain comes harder later. Let’s talk quietly over tea next week—same place, same time."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—calm on the surface, but the wind shifts in ways that make you wonder if something’s brewing behind the clouds. The old trees still stand firm, but even they’re whispering about roots running deeper than we thought. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—patience is the only tool we can trust right now."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm that hasn’t decided whether to break or pass. The usual rhythms are still there, but the pauses between them are longer, and no one’s sure what’s coming next. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we’re all watching the same sky."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
